A short novel by the Senegalese writer Mariama Ba, published in French in 1979, written as a letter from a widow, Ramatoulaye, to her friend after her husband took a second, younger wife.

It weighs Islam, tradition, marriage, class and the hopes of the first generation of educated women in independent Senegal. It won the first Noma Award for Publishing in Africa in 1980 and has been translated into many languages. It is read in schools across Africa and in courses on African and women's writing. Ba died in 1981 before her second novel appeared. See also Senghor and African literature in French.
